main_text.l: JOHANNIS BUXTORFI LEXICON HEBRAICUM ET CHALDAICUM:
[?]אָבַב Nomen masc. Culmus, Spica mutica, Exod.9.31. Arista virens, Lev.2.14. Inde mensis אָבִיב Exod.13.4. id est; Martius, quasi mensis Spicarum, quia bordeum tunc fuit spicatum, Exod.9.31.
אָב m. Viror, Virens, Fructus recens, forma ip. : Cum Affixo, בְּאָבִו In virore suo, Job.8.12. Plurale constructum, בְּאָבֵי הַנַּחַל In virentia vallis, Cant.6.10.

אָבָא, אָנְבָא m. Chald. Idem. Aff. וּבְדְרוּ אָנְבִיָּה Et dispergite fructum ejus; Dan.4.11. וְאָנְבָּה Et recens fructus ejus, Dan.4.9. ubi ה est loco Dagesch. Radix אָבָא Primum vel praecocem fructum producere; legitur in Targum; Hos.9.10.

אָבַד Periit, Interiit: Partic. Benoni; אֹבֵד Periens, vel Perdita, Deut.32.28. in Pathach, propter constructionem, ut Aben Esra recensét: Futur. יֹאבַד Peribit, Proverb.19.9. in Tzere propter pausam: Chald. Futur. יֶאבְדוּ Peribunt, Jerem.10.v.11. Pih. אִבֵּד Perire fecit,

The large opening Hebrew word of the first entry is printed in bold and its vowels are hard to read at this scan size: marked [?]. Vowel points in the Hebrew throughout are approximated from the scan and may not be exact. Ornament band and the small letter "א" as a section marker are not printed text in the usual sense; the letter is kept as

. The title words are set in large spaced capitals and are treated as one level-1 heading for the work. The Hebrew "Culmus, Spica mutica" is printed without a diacritic over the final a, transcribed as plain "mutica". Gathering signature "A" is at the foot. Greek and Hebrew copied in Hebrew letters; the Latin printed "Fructus" with a ligature for "ct", transcribed as "Fructus".
